name: Jackson §5.15: Faraday's law
description: Jackson §5.15: a changing magnetic flux induces an electric field that circulates around it, $\oint \mathbf{E}\cdot d\mathbf{l} = -d\Phi/dt$. The current in this coil rises steadily; no charge is anywhere near the particle at rest, yet the induced field drives it around the axis, faster and faster, while the growing field tightens its orbit. Bring it into the detector with at least 0.3 of kinetic energy: only the induction can give it that much.

reality.represents: Faraday's law: an electric field induced by a rising current (Jackson §5.15)

remarks.detail: The changing flux drives the particle around the axis with no charge nearby, and the growing field tightens its orbit (the flux through it is an adiabatic invariant, §12.5).
The field follows the current at once (c = ∞ for the motion); a real coil is quasi-static too as long as it is much smaller than a wavelength.

remarks.line: A coil is one thin loop
remarks.detail: The coil is a single loop of thin wire carrying a steady current, its field the exact Biot–Savart field (perpendicular to the plane in it, and far from uniform); a real magnet has many turns, iron and pole pieces shaped for a uniform field.
